newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - PHILIPPINE NEWSPAPERS - AUG 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - PHILIPPINE NEWSPAPERS - AUG 7.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Ramos accepts with deep regret the resignation of Defence Secretary Renato de Villa effective September 15, giving him 40 more days to complete his programme before pursuing his presidential ambition. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- A Korean Airline jet full of honeymooners and tourists crashes in a dense jungle on the Pacific island of Guam, killing most of the 254 people aboard, officials said. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- Nine suspected car thieves, desperately trying to evade car arrest, gun down a business executive-motorist and a policeman and injures two other law enforcers through the peak morning traffic along a main road in Manila. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- The Securities and Exchange Commission strips the Philippine Stock Exchange president of power to investigate cases against brokers and listed firms. The power has been transferred to the exhange's compliance and surveillance department.(MALAYA/JOURNAL)

- The central bank will lower today its key overnight borrowing and lending rates to 18 percent and 22 percent respectively in a move seen to signal the continued normalisation of the local currency market. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- President Ramos says the expected impact on inflation of the El Nino weather phenomenon in the coming lean months, coupled with the lingering effects of the peso depreciation, are bothering him. (BUSINESSWORLD)
